tasks.title: The story and epic contracts, at the routes that author them
tasks.objective: Extract check_story_contract(item, known_epics) and check_epic_contract(epic) in forge_cli/roadmap.py and call them from cmd_derive, cmd_import and cmd_add, leaving save_roadmap and the status routes on the weaker check_item.
acceptance_criteria: check_story_contract refuses a story that omits epic, story narrative, acceptance_criteria, skill, or depends_on, and names every missing field rather than the first.
depends_on must be present even when empty: [] is accepted and a missing key is refused, so 'no dependencies' is stated rather than inferred from absence.
check_story_contract refuses an epic id that is not in the known epics of the same payload or the stored roadmap.
check_epic_contract requires id, title, objective, and source_refs that resolve to existing repo-relative paths; a source_ref pointing at a missing file is refused.

cmd_derive, cmd_import and cmd_add all call both contracts; save_roadmap, mark_status, cmd_assign, cmd_link_spec and cmd_heal do not, and a legacy roadmap whose stories have no epic still loads, flips status, and heals.
check_item keeps its existing type checks unchanged, so the two concerns stay separable.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "roadmap or epic or story_contract"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That validation lands only on the three authoring routes. cmd_heal runs at the post-merge moment a roadmap is least well-formed, and gating it would remove the recovery path exactly when it is needed.

tasks.title: Two epic routes, and --epic required on add
tasks.objective: Add forge roadmap epic add and forge roadmap set-epic, and require --epic on roadmap add, so that requiring a known epic does not lock the roadmap against its own backfill.
acceptance_criteria: roadmap epic add <id> --title --objective --source-ref (repeatable) writes an epic through save_roadmap's existing epics parameter, requires sign-off, and refuses a duplicate id.
roadmap epic add does NOT require the epics-approved decision, because it appends one epic where import replaces the whole list; the asymmetry is stated in the command help.
roadmap set-epic <story-key> --epic <id> writes the epic field on an existing story, refusing an unknown story key and an unknown epic id.
roadmap add requires --epic and refuses an unknown epic id.
roadmap add --no-spec --reason still produces a story with origin: adhoc and spec_debt_reason set, and that path has a test it did not have before.
Duplicate story keys, self-dependencies and cycles remain refused at add.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "epic_add or set_epic or roadmap_add or no_spec"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the --no-spec carve-out survives intact. Decision 0014 puts authorization at plan save, and plans.py already refuses spec-debt stories, so removing the hatch would delete a designed path rather than close a hole.

tasks.title: Schema note, the ordering decision, and an advisory doctor report
tasks.objective: State the required story fields in factory/schemas/roadmap.json's item_fields_note, land the derived-ordering decision record, and report epic-less legacy roadmaps in forge doctor without incrementing its failure count.
acceptance_criteria: item_fields_note names epic, story, acceptance_criteria, skill and depends_on as required at the authoring routes, and says which routes those are.
forge doctor prints an advisory line for a roadmap with no epics, and for a story with no epic, in the same [opt ] form the capture checks use.
The advisory lines never increment doctor's failure count, so a legacy project is told without being blocked.
docs/decisions/0021-derived-ordering.md is present and referenced by the PH-2 plan; it stays status: proposed until a human confirms it.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "doctor or roadmap_schema"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the doctor lines are advisory in fact and not just in wording — a legacy project must still be able to run every gate it could run before.

tasks.title: Backfill this repo's own roadmap through the new routes
tasks.objective: Give plans/roadmap.json an epic and point its stories at it using epic add and set-epic, so the routes are exercised by the repo that ships them.
acceptance_criteria: plans/roadmap.json carries at least one epic with id, title, objective and resolving source_refs.
Every story in plans/roadmap.json names a known epic.
The backfill is performed by running forge roadmap epic add and forge roadmap set-epic, not by editing the JSON; the commands used are recorded in the commit message.
forge roadmap list, forge roadmap parallel and forge doctor all still work against the backfilled roadmap, and doctor no longer prints the epic-less advisory for this repo.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "roadmap"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the backfill went through the commands. A hand-edited roadmap would pass the same tests while proving nothing about the routes this story exists to add.
